newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK money rates down, govt paper yields mostly up.
newsitem.headline: HK money rates down, govt paper yields mostly up.

text.p: Interbank rates were easier in quiet trading on Tuesday as the market was liquid after a Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) injection on Monday and bank offers of short-dates, dealers said.
An HKMA executive said the authority injected a total of HK$1.9 billion into the market on Monday.
Overnight money eased to 4-1/2 3/8 percent from 5-1/4 1/8 and three-month money was 5-9/16 1/2 against 5-5/8 9/16.
"The market is cash rich after the injection and traders started to offer short-dates after feeling more comfortable with the RTGS," one dealer said.
But dealers said trading was still quiet as traders tended to trim down transactions in December for the implementation of the Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system which started on Monday.
"The operation of RTGS is so far so good and some banks, which realised they hold more bills than they needed for repo, began to sell short-dates," a European bank dealer said.

Under the new settlement system, the government's Exchange Fund bills and notes can be used by banks to obtain interest-free intraday liquidity by carrying out repurchase (repo) transactions with the HKMA.
